description.narrative:
This project aims to remove all illegal invaders from the legally recognised Awa indigenous land which was demarcated in 2005, and create and implement effective measures to protect the land from future invasions, so that the Awa can live sustainably and free from external threats. Survival International aims to achieve this by launching a worldwide campaign to raise global awareness of the situation of the Awa, and lobby the Brazilian federal government to reinstate the federal judge ruling of 2009 to remove all invaders in the area. Activities will include the utilisation of new media, networking, and producing and disseminating a short film on the situation of the Awa to rally public and governmental support.
This project is important because there are currently only 350 Awa living in four settled communities, and a further 60-100 Awa living in small uncontacted groups in the forest and in demarcated areas, who risk their lives due to external threats to their land and livelihoods. Threats include: the existence of three fixed colonist settlements, and the presence of illegal loggers, settlers and ranchers in the forest which are jeopardising the Awa's ability to have sustainable livelihoods through hunting and gathering in the forest; their health is at risk due to exposure to foreign diseases from these invaders; and the environment is threatened by deforestation and the resulting impact on climate change. In 2009 a federal judge ruling was passed to remove the illegal invaders from the Awa lands, but this has since been appealed by ranchers and invaders who remain there. Despite the fact that Brazil ratified the ILO convention 169 in 2002 to protect indigenous rights, this project is needed to lobby the government to respect and protect the Awa's rights to their land, and to prevent the further loss of life of this threatened community.
